transcript.content:
hey, i'm berry

tell me your dream, however it comes back to you
oh hey. so I was at this night market with my older sister, and it was packed, like hundreds of people. there were strings of little yellow lights over the stalls. that part really stuck with me.

the little yellow lights, yeah. those feel like the kind of detail that stays with you for a while

what else do you remember?

we stopped at a fish stall because my sister wanted to buy fish. there was an old man with fish laid out on ice. one of them looked at me and said my name. it was silver and about as long as my arm. no one else seemed to hear it.

that's so strange, a fish knowing your name and no one else hearing it

what did it feel like when it said your name?
honestly it was quiet, like it was just for me. I didn't feel scared, more like I was supposed to hear it. the old man wrapped it in newspaper and handed it to me, and I held it against my chest.

that feels important, holding it like that

did you get a sense of why you were supposed to hear it?

no idea. it just said my name again later. we were leaving the market on one bicycle, my sister pedalling and me on the back holding the fish. it started to rain, big warm drops. the market lights were behind us. that's when it said my name again, quietly, and I woke up.

the warm rain and the lights behind you, that's a whole feeling

if you could pause the dream right at one moment, which one would it be?
probably the part with the silver fish on the ice, right before the old man wrapped it. that look it gave me. everything else kind of moves past fast, but that one stayed still.

so you were at a night market with your sister, packed with people, and there were those little yellow lights over the stalls. you stopped at a fish stall, and one silver fish about as long as your arm looked at you and said your name. it felt quiet, like it was just for you, not scary, and no one else heard it. the old man wrapped it in newspaper and handed it to you, and you held it against your chest. later you were leaving on one bicycle, your sister pedalling, you on the back holding the fish. warm rain was falling and the market lights were behind you, and the fish said your name again quietly, and then you woke up. the moment that stayed with you was the fish on the ice, right before the old man wrapped it, that look it gave you.

did i get that right, or did i miss anything?
yeah, that's right. you got it.
would you like to see it drawn?
yes, that would be cool.

there are a few ways it could be drawn. a soft pencil and charcoal drawing, with soft strokes and smudged shadows, would feel like a tender, quiet memory. an old photograph, sepia-toned, with warm sepia tones and gentle aging, would feel like a cherished memory from long ago. ink lines with soft watercolour, with delicate ink lines and pale washes, would feel like a page from a dream journal, both precise and fading. a photograph, as you saw it, with true-to-life colours and sharp focus, would feel like standing right back in that moment.

which of those feels closest to you, or would you describe it your own way?
probably the ink lines with soft watercolor. that feels closest, like it's precise but also kind of fading, like a dream journal.

okay, i'll start with the old man

i picture him weathered, from years at that stall, my guess. hands that have handled fish a long time

does that sound like him to you, or would you change anything? or i can just go with it if you'd rather leave it to me
that sounds right. the dream doesn't say much about him, just that he was old and had fish laid out on ice. go with your guess.

ok, i'll go with that weathered old man

what was she like in the dream, anything about her that stands out?
she was just my older sister. the dream doesn't really describe her looks. she wanted to buy fish, and she was the one pedalling the bicycle. that's all I remember.

ok, sketching the old man, your sister, the silver fish, the road away from the market, the bicycle, and the newspaper wrapping now. just those, nothing else yet, they'll appear on the right.

and here's how i'm picturing the night market on its own, from what you told me: strings of little yellow lights over the stalls, and the fish stall with the fish laid out on ice. for the rest, these are my guesses: an outdoor market, crowded, with many stalls, probably long rows or a square under the night sky. the little yellow lights make a warm glow, and the crowd is in and out of shadow.

does anything about the night market feel different from that, or would you rather leave it to me?
that sounds right, the yellow lights and the fish stall are the main things. the rest is kind of a blur, so go with what you said.

ok, i'll keep the night market as i described

the fish was silver and about an arm's length. was it just plain silver, or did it have any other colours or markings?
just plain silver, as far as I remember. nothing else about it.

ok, sketching the night market now, it'll appear on the right. nothing else is being drawn yet.

i'll draw you too, since you're in it. how would you like to be drawn: as you are, maybe you can tell me a little about yourself, or however i imagine you?
you can draw me however you imagine. the dream doesn't say how I looked.
ok, i'm sketching everything now. it'll all appear on the right over the next minute or two. you can say if anything looks wrong once it's there.

i can't actually see the pictures, but from what you've described it sounds right. the only things the dream really pinned down were the silver fish, the old man, the yellow lights, the stall with fish on ice, my sister, me, the bicycle, the newspaper, and the road away from the market. nothing else was really fixed.
does it look the way you remember?
from what you've said, it sounds like it fits. i don't see any wrong details.
ok, then i'll draw the moments of the dream in order, each one carrying on from the ones before. they'll appear on the right as they're ready.
got it. i'll wait to see the rest.

so far only one of the six moments is up on the right, you and your sister walking through the packed market. and i couldn't draw the moment with the fish still in newspaper against your chest, there was a problem on our side, i'm sorry about that.

does that walking moment look the way you remember?

it sounds okay from what you said, but the dream didn't describe us walking in much detail. just that it was crowded and there were strings of little yellow lights over the stalls. so if that's in there, it's right.
the crowd and the yellow lights are definitely in there, so it should feel right. the other moments are still being drawn, they'll come along.
okay, I'm sure it'll come together. thanks for doing this.

glad you're feeling good about it. two of the six moments are up now, the walk through the market and your sister stopping at the fish stall, the old man there. the rest are still coming.

does the moment with your sister stopping at the fish stall look the way you remember?
hard to say without seeing it, but if it shows her at the stall with the old man and the fish on ice, that's the important part. the dream didn't add much detail beyond that.

that's the important part, and it's there on the right, her at the stall with the old man and the fish on ice.

the rest of the moments are still being drawn, they'll come along soon.
alright, sounds good.
the silver fish looking straight at you and saying your name quietly is up on the right now, on the ice, and no one else reacts. does that look the way you saw it?
from your description, yeah. the fish was silver, about as long as my arm, and the old man wrapped it in newspaper right after. if it shows it looking at me quietly, that's how it felt.
glad that feels right. the rest of the moments are still being drawn, they'll come along.
okay, still here.
does the moment with the old man wrapping the silver fish in newspaper look the way you remember?
if it's the old man wrapping the silver fish in newspaper, that's right. the dream just had me holding it against my chest after that. nothing else to add.
that's good, the old man wrapping the silver fish in newspaper is up on the right. the rest of the moments are still being drawn, they'll come along soon.
alright, waiting for the last one.

that's the last of the moments i could draw, the sister pedalling the bicycle with you on the back holding the fish is up on the right now

does that look the way you remember?
if it shows us on one bicycle, her pedalling and me on the back holding the fish, that's exactly it. the dream didn't say much else about that part.

glad that last moment feels right, that's all the moments done now

five of the six are up on the right. the one with the fish still in newspaper against your chest couldn't be drawn, i'm sorry about that. thank you for sharing your dream with me, you can look through the pictures there
